title: Are MCPs just deadweight now?
author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
selftext: Watched a video recently that was saying frontier (Astra/Opus 5.5) models run faster and with less token spend through CLI now. I’m specifically talking for Unity and Blender work here. Has anyone that has stopped using MCP found this to be true? Are you losing any functionality by not using an MCP these day?

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
Well with the unity CLI you don't really need the unity mcp anymore. Most things are done easier and quicker by having the agent use the cli. 

There are still use cases for building our custom tools on MCP. Like a batch screenshot of scene view tool and such. But in general CLI is better option for most things.

replies.author: hello-xworld
replies.body:
CLI = Command line interface  
MCP = Model Context Provider

CLI is where you run commands directly into bash/terminal. It’s what AI models use under the hood. Programmers have been using it for ages because it gives you access to more functionality on your computer.

MCP is a context provider so your agents has access to a specific software on your computer. Some software offer both CLI and MCP, some offer only one.

Unity offers both CLI and MCP access. Figma only offer MCP.

You don’t really need to learn the nuances of each, just understand that if a software offers both, then it might be beneficial to use one over the other, but it all depends.

replies.body: You’re right! Ugh I keep getting it mixed up with provider hehe

replies.author: GreenBlueStar
replies.body: MCP think of it like an external plugin for an AI  model to use so it understands the context for whatever function it needs to work with. But if that function is in-built into the AI's model already, for example, if it can just use the CLI of this external tool, it doesn't need the specific MCP functionality anymore since it can just figure out how that tool works. Model Context Provider.

comments.author: MattMaxBuilds
comments.body:
I started building MCPs in 2025 as basically a side quest at work. I was building an AI platform on top of the systems I was already responsible for, so I wrote my own MCPs for Snowflake, Salesforce, and Atlassian instead of just taking the official offerings as-is. I thought I could build them better for the actual use case, and it worked. I also forked and extended several AWS Labs MCPs, ran MCP serverlessly on Graviton, and had to work around some of the session/state assumptions at the time. I eventually got all of that deployed inside a multibillion-dollar company, completely solo. I had no help on any of it.

More relevant here, Kiln is my newer independent work. It’s an open-source procedural 3D system where coding agents can use MCP to generate, inspect, revise, and save editable 3D assets. Instead of MCP just being a wrapper around some SaaS API, the model is using it as part of a visual feedback loop with a 3D environment. That’s the direction I find a lot more interesting for game dev.

MCP itself is good. A lot of people just treat it like “API calls, but for agents,” then wonder why it feels clunky. It’s extensible, the spec keeps improving, and there’s a lot more you can do with it if you actually understand why it exists.

comments.author: New_Patience_8107
comments.body:
I think they do different things for different folks.

Mcp is more the human layer. You're logged in on Claude Co work or codex or something orchestrating from the front end across different tools.

The CLI is more for agentic coding. It uses the combo of tools and skills for the specific vendors it's supposed to interact with. An MCP server just floods contest you don't necessarily need.

comments.author: DeniedWorks
comments.body: The standard for how MCP servers work changed recently as well. But yes if a company makes a CLI interface for agents, it will be extremely efficient.

comments.author: Izolight

This is one thing I am trying to find out, especially which models work well with mcp and which are better without and also across different harnesses.

For this I made a benchmark website where you can compare and vote on different model, harness, reasoning configurations. I am continuously adding new runs as new models come out and to fill some comparison gaps, but it's getting hard to keep up lately with so many releases (without spending too much).

Check it out at http://render-arena.izolight.xyz/

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
For CLI you need an environment the CLI runs in, and that's mostly for developers using Codex or Claude Code.   
CLI usage was there first before MCP existed, so there are good reason for introducing MCP.

  
MCP is still the thing to use for everybody else, even on the web in a normal chat session. You need a standard too for things to integrate well. Also it solves authentication universally.

CLI is also normally very powerful and thus difficult to fully secure, compared to MCP usage.
